ch16.d.mode: A single pulse or a continuous sine wave
ch16.d.end: Fixed: tied to a wall. Free: a ring sliding on a frictionless rod
ch16.d.lambda: Wavelength $\lambda$ of the continuous wave; the wave speed $v$ stays the same
ch16.d.parts: Incident wave (blue dashed) and reflected wave (orange dashed); solid black = their sum (the actual string)
ch16.goal.reflect: A travelling wave reflects at the end of the string: inverted at a fixed end, upright at a free end
ch16.goal.standing: Incident and reflected waves of the same frequency overlap into a standing wave with nodes and antinodes that stay in place
ch16.obs.fixed: Pulse, fixed end: the reflected pulse comes back upside down; the end never moves
ch16.obs.free: Pulse, free end: the pulse comes back upright; at the moment of reflection the end rises to twice the pulse height
ch16.obs.sum: Black string = blue dashed + orange dashed (superposition)
ch16.obs.nodes: Continuous wave: nodes (black dots) appear where the reflected wave has arrived and stay put; node spacing $\lambda/2$
ch16.obs.freeNodes: Fixed end: the end is a node. Free end: the end is an antinode, the first node is $\lambda/4$ from it
ch16.assume.ideal: Uniform, inextensible string, no energy loss, $v = 2\ \text{m/s}$
ch16.assume.left: The left side is part of a long string: the reflected wave leaves to the left and does not reflect again
ch16.r.d.f: Frequency $f$ at which the left end is shaken; drag slowly to sweep it
ch16.r.d.env: Steady-state amplitude envelope (grey dashed) and node positions (black dots)
ch16.r.goal.res: String fixed at both ends: the amplitude grows large only at $f_n = nv/2L$, where $L = n\lambda/2$ (resonance)
ch16.r.goal.modes: The resonant frequencies are set by the length of the string and the wave speed: $f_n = n f_1$
ch16.r.obs.default: Default 2 Hz $= f_2$: a standing wave with 3 nodes (ends included) and 2 antinodes grows steadily
ch16.r.obs.off: 1.5 Hz: the amplitude stays near the driving amplitude; $2L/\lambda$ is not an integer
ch16.r.obs.sweep: Raise the frequency in small steps and watch the dot on the graph: peaks only at 1, 2, 3 and 4 Hz
ch16.r.obs.nodes: At $f_n$ the number of antinodes is $n = 2L/\lambda$
ch16.r.obs.build: Right after switching to a resonant frequency the amplitude does not jump; it builds up over a few seconds
ch16.r.assume.string: String length $L = 2\ \text{m}$, wave speed $v = 4\ \text{m/s}$, driving amplitude 3 cm; the driven end is nearly a node
ch16.r.assume.damp: Weak damping (rate $0.3\ \text{s}^{-1}$) keeps the amplitude finite at resonance. The curve on the graph is the steady-state amplitude
